correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the coefficient ratio inequalities: \(a_i/\widetilde a_i=\beta/L_i\ge\beta/L_0>1\), and \((1+\beta x_i)/(1+L_i x_i)\ge(1+\beta x_0)/(1+L_0x_0)>1\) using monotonicity for \(x_i\ge x_0\), \(1\le L_i\le L_0\). Both coefficient sequences therefore dominate by \(q\). With the source comparison \(\widetilde\Delta_i^{(4)}\ge\widetilde\Delta_i^{(2)}\), initial \(\Delta_1^{(2)}=\widetilde\Delta_1^{(2)}\), and \(\Delta_1^{(4)}\ge q\widetilde\Delta_1^{(4)}\), a two-component induction gives \(\Delta_m^{(2)}\ge p^{m-1}\widetilde\Delta_m^{(2)}\) and \(\Delta_m^{(4)}\ge qp^{m-1}\widetilde\Delta_m^{(4)}\). The necessary identities \((p-1)/(q-p)=\delta\) and \(\widetilde b_i/\widetilde a_i>d_i\ge\delta\) were checked symbolically. Passage to logarithmic growth yields the stated positive rate; it does not imply the stronger advertised rate. The uninspected source-specific inequality is stated transparently as an external premise whose verification remains an access risk.

final_claim: For the three-dimensional ellipsoidal open-billiard family in Al Dowais--Stoyanov with \(\beta>c_1^{-2}\), the two scalar coefficient recurrences admit a strictly positive comparison rate \(\lambda_1(\beta)-\lambda_2\ge\log p>0\), where \(\delta=d_0-2r_0\), \(L_0=c_1^{-2}\), \(x_0=2c_1\delta/r_0\), \(q=\min\{\beta/L_0,(1+\beta x_0)/(1+L_0x_0)\}\), and \(p=(1+\delta q)/(1+\delta)\). This repairs a coefficient-comparison argument for strict splitting, without establishing the stronger rate claimed in the initiating preprint.
limitations: Applies only to the specified congruent-ellipsoid and two-unstable-exponent setting.

The full October 2026 preprint was not independently accessible in this execution; some source-specific auxiliary comparisons therefore remain a documented premise rather than independently rederived from billiard geometry.
Does not claim the printed stronger bound \(\log(\beta c_1^2)\) is false.
